author: CHLOE KUCERA
title: First responders commended for lifesaving actions - NewsBreak
text:
By CHLOE KUCERA ,
11 hours ago
A series of emergency incidents between mid-February and mid-March prompted local officials to publicly recognize the actions of police officers, deputies and dispatchers during Tuesday’s Faribault City Council meeting.
“This isn’t something we normally do during a presentation before the council,” FPD Chief John Sherwin said at the beginning of the meeting. “But we had a really good run between mid-February and mid-March and I felt it necessary to recognize the actions of officers involved.”
Sherwin noted that many of those being honored do not seek recognition, adding that their work often goes unnoticed.
“When I first became a police officer, I had a lieutenant that told me the bravest thing you will do is take your oath of office, because everything else is just doing your job,” he said. “But their actions were such that I think they need to be recognized.”
Stabbing response saves life
The first incident occurred March 6, when Faribault police officers and Rice County Sheriff’s deputies responded to a stabbing.
The victim was unresponsive and had lost a significant amount of blood. A flight nurse later reported the individual’s blood pressure was 40 over zero, indicating they were in near-fatal condition.
Officer John Wunderlich was first on scene and quickly applied a tourniquet. Deputies Ben Borash and Jesse Lee assisted, applying a second tourniquet and helping stabilize the victim.
Due to foggy conditions, a medical helicopter was unavailable. Sherwin said the quick actions of responders were crucial in saving the victim’s life.
Wunderlich and Borash received lifesaving awards, while Lee received a commendation.
Investigation protects juvenile
On March 12, officer Nick Smith responded to a report of a missing juvenile. During the investigation, Smith uncovered evidence that the juvenile was being solicited for sexual activity online.
Using available technology and investigative tools, Smith developed a suspect profile for detectives while ensuring the juvenile’s safety.
For his efforts, Smith received a written commendation.
Officers respond to medical emergency
On Feb. 16, officers Nick Smith and Angel Perez responded to a life-threatening medical call involving an unconscious individual with an obstructed airway.
The officers began lifesaving measures, and with assistance from firefighters and paramedics, the obstruction was cleared and the victim’s condition improved.
Both Smith and Perez received lifesaving awards.
House fire rescue earns top honor
Multiple responders were recognized for their actions during a Feb. 18 house fire.
A 911 caller reported a family trapped on the second floor of a burning home. Dispatcher Atlanta Schultz quickly relayed important information to police and fire units.
Smith was first to arrive and found the home heavily engulfed in flames. He discovered the family had escaped to the roof but remained trapped.
Smith directed a resident to move a pickup truck beneath the roof. Officers Perez and Kevin Fisher arrived shortly after and helped coordinate the rescue, lowering the family members onto the truck bed to safety.
Moments later, a propane tank exploded at the front of the home.
For his quick thinking and actions, Smith received the department’s Medal of Merit. Perez and Fisher, along with Schultz, received written commendations.
Mayor Tom Spooner closed the recognition by thanking the first responders for their service.
“I speak for everyone up here on the council, thank you to law enforcement and all first responders for all you do,” he said.
